messages:
hina: Quick UX review: compact compare quick-actions feel cluttered. Considering moving less-used actions into a contextual menu. Link to frames: https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE

lucas: Strong agree. Quick-actions should be 1-2 primary (compare, pin), others in overflow. Also consider long-press on mobile to reveal extra actions.

maria: We need to ensure keyboard access for overflow items. Can't hide important actions behind hover.

ethan: Microcopy nit: 'Pin version' vs 'Pin to compare' - which phrasing communicates persistence? Research suggests 'Pin version' is clearer.

claire: Accessibility: overflow menu needs aria-haspopup and aria-expanded. Menu items should be buttons with role=menuitem and keyboard traps avoided.

ux-bot: Usability heuristic check: minimal visible actions, progressive disclosure, and clear affordance for pinned items.

hina: Proposal: primary actions = [Pin, Compare], secondary = [View changelog, Open in sandbox, Evaluate]. Secondary moves into overflow labeled 'More actions'.

lucas: Visual idea: reduce action density by using icon-only buttons with accessible labels. Provide persistent tooltip on hover for desktop.

maria: Also check that pin persistence settings align with other catalog pages (we decided per-user per-catalog previously). Confirming.

ethan: For the 'Evaluate' action, let's gate it behind a permission check and grey-out with tooltip 'Requires evaluation credits' if not allowed.

claire: Focus-handling when menu opens: focus should move into the menu and trap until closed with Escape or click away. Menu should return focus to the action button when closed.

hina: Decision: move less-used actions to overflow, keep Pin+Compare visible, icon-only with tooltips & a11y labels, menu accessible and focus-managed.

lucas: I'll update the comps and provide the interaction spec. maria: I'll confirm copy consistency across catalog pages. ux-bot: Add task to the backlog for a11y audit on the action menu.

maria: One more thing: try to limit badges per-row to 3 at most. Maybe order them: pinned highlight > perf > reliability > stale (overflow).

hina: Good constraint. Closing 44d
